newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Maverick politician says she has had death threats.
newsitem.headline: Maverick politician says she has had death threats.

text.p: A maverick Australian politician who sparked a heated race debate now engulfing the country said on Saturday she had received death threats.

"These sorts of things are just private and I am just keeping these things very close to me -- not taking notice of these death threats," Pauline Hanson, an independent member of Parliament, told reporters in Brisbane.
"I won't be threatened. I won't be intimidated," she said.

The Courier Mail newspaper in Brisbane on Saturday reported that police were investigating a threatening letter warning Hanson she would be killed and that a contract had been placed on her, possibly by a Vietnamese gang involved in drugs.
The newspaper said the letter warned Hanson she could be killed like Sydney politican John Newman.

Newman, 47, a politican in Sydney's western suburbs, was shot twice in the chest by a drive-by assassin on September 5, 1994. Police investigations into his murder are believed to centre on his stance against Asian crime gangs in Australia, particularly in his own electorate.
Hanson's Brisbane electorate has a large Vietnamese community.
Police refused to confirm or deny the Courier Mail report.
In her maiden parliamentary speech last month, Hanson called for an end to Asian immigration, claiming Australia was being swamped by Asian migrants.
She also said that Aborigines, the most disadvantaged in Australian society, received priviledged treatment.
Asians make up about a quarter of the 100,000 migrants which enter Australia each year.
Hanson's comments have sparked a debate on immigration and race in Australia, which at times has been xenophobic.
